notes:
A type of traditional Japanese dwelling where multiple housing units share continuous walls under one long roof. Composed of {長|なが} (long) and ⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ (building, house). They were the standard housing for commoners in Edo-period cities and symbolize the tight-knit community life of that era.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長屋|ながや}{暮|ぐ}らし: tenement living
- {長屋|ながや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{住人|じゅうにん}→住人：11611_juunin⟧: tenement residents
- {長屋|ながや}{門|もん}: long gate (a type of gate building)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{長屋|ながや} are a fixture of ⟦{落語|らくご}→落語：04457_rakugo⟧ (traditional comic storytelling), where they serve as the setting for humorous tales of Edo-period commoners. The expression {長屋|ながや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧ is a famous ⟦{落語|らくご}→落語：04457_rakugo⟧ story about tenement dwellers improvising a cherry blossom viewing party.
